This is the workroom macOS app repo (macapp/ dir), a SwiftUI app with embedded Ghostty terminal panes in a tab strip. I'm planning GitHub issue #141: "Favicons for terminals and what they are currently running" — the idea is terminal tabs should show an icon (like a browser favicon) representing what's currently running in that pane (e.g. running `claude` shows the Claude logo in the tab, similar to how Codex/other CLIs might get their own icon).

I need a comprehensive map of the current tab UI and process-detection machinery so I can plan where a "favicon" feature would slot in. Please investigate and report:

1. **Tab strip / tab view UI**: Where is the tab bar/strip SwiftUI view defined? What does each tab currently show (title, icon, busy/spinner indicator, close button)? File paths + line numbers for the view struct and its icon-rendering subview.

2. **Existing "what's running" / foreground process detection**: The memory system mentions "Agent OSC 9;4 cadence" (Claude emits OSC 9;4 once at start/end, Codex never — both animate a title spinner) and a "Session-daemon reattach foreground detection" fix (foreground-pgid + argv0 detection, not proc_name). Find:
   - Where foreground process / argv0 / pgid is currently tracked per pane/session (daemon-side and/or app-side Swift). File paths + line numbers.
   - Where OSC 9;4 escape sequences are parsed/handled, and where the "busy indicator" / spinner animation state lives (e.g. an `isBusy` or `agentBusy` property, what view renders the spinner).
   - Is there already any concept of "which CLI tool is running" (e.g. distinguishing `claude` vs `codex` vs plain shell) anywhere in the codebase — session title, OSC 7/2 title parsing, or elsewhere?

3. **Existing icon/asset infrastructure**: How are icons currently sourced for tabs/UI (SF Symbols vs bundled image assets)? Is there anywhere in the codebase that already maps a command/tool name to a logo/icon (e.g. for a "run" skill, app switcher, or elsewhere)? Check macapp/Resources for any bundled logos (Claude, Codex, etc).

4. **Session/pane model**: What Swift type represents a single terminal pane/session (e.g. GhosttySurfaceView, a Session/Pane model struct)? Where would a computed "current running tool" property naturally live, and how is that model wired to the tab strip view (data flow, ObservableObject/@Observable, bindings)?

Report file:line references throughout. Keep the report organized under these 4 headings. This is investigation only — do not propose the implementation, just map the existing code precisely so planning can happen with accurate file/line citations.

```swift
import AppKit

/// One curated entry (issue #141): identifies a CLI/TUI by its exec'd basename (or, for tools that
/// rewrite their own title, a literal provider title) and names the bundled `ToolLogo-<id>` imageset
/// carrying its real brand favicon. Loaded from Resources/tool-logos/registry.json — the SAME file
/// Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh reads to know what to fetch, so the fetch list and the match list
/// can't drift apart.
struct ToolLogoEntry: Codable, Equatable {
  let id: String
  let displayName: String
  let executables: [String]
  let titles: [String]?       // provider-owned literal titles (e.g. "claude code"); rare
  let faviconSource: String   // consumed only by the fetch script; decoded here too, unused at runtime
}

/// Latched onto a running terminal tab (mirrors `AgentBackend`, but data-driven and not limited to
/// two cases). Deliberately smaller than `ToolLogoEntry` — a tab only needs to remember the match.
struct RecognizedTool: Equatable {
  let id: String
  let displayName: String
}

enum ToolLogoRegistry {
  static let entries: [ToolLogoEntry] = loadEntries()

  private static let byExecutable: [String: ToolLogoEntry] = {
    var map: [String: ToolLogoEntry] = [:]
    for entry in entries { for exe in entry.executables { map[exe] = entry } }
    return map
  }()

  private static let byTitle: [String: ToolLogoEntry] = {
    var map: [String: ToolLogoEntry] = [:]
    for entry in entries { for t in entry.titles ?? [] { map[t.lowercased()] = entry } }
    return map
  }()

  /// Pure data match — works even before `fetch-tool-logos.sh` has produced an imageset for the id,
  /// so it's directly unit-testable against registry.json content alone.
  ///
  /// Case-sensitive on purpose, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition.backend(for:)`
  /// (AgentUsage.swift:105-126): a command title is the real, lower-case executable name, so
  /// comparing case-sensitively rejects prose like "Go to definition" matching the `go` entry.
  /// DO NOT `.lowercased()` this side — that regression multiplies with ~30 registry entries.
  static func matchingEntry(forTitle title: String?) -> ToolLogoEntry? {
    guard let title else { return nil }
    let trimmed = title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
    guard !trimmed.isEmpty else { return nil }
    if let literal = byTitle[trimmed.lowercased()] { return literal }
    guard let first = trimmed.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).first else { return nil }
    let token = String(first).trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "\"'"))
    return byExecutable[(token as NSString).lastPathComponent]
  }

  static func matchingEntry(forExecutableName name: String?) -> ToolLogoEntry? {
    guard let name else { return nil }
    return byExecutable[(name as NSString).lastPathComponent]
  }

  /// The gate production call sites actually use: nil unless the id's real logo made it into
  /// Assets.xcassets. A registry.json entry can exist before the fetch script has been run for it
  /// (or a fetch failed for one tool) — this must never surface a broken/blank image.
  static func tool(forTitle title: String?) -> RecognizedTool? {
    matchingEntry(forTitle: title).flatMap(recognizedIfBundled)
  }
  static func tool(forExecutableName name: String?) -> RecognizedTool? {
    matchingEntry(forExecutableName: name).flatMap(recognizedIfBundled)
  }

  static func assetName(for id: String) -> String { "ToolLogo-\(id)" }

  private static func recognizedIfBundled(_ entry: ToolLogoEntry) -> RecognizedTool? {
    guard NSImage(named: assetName(for: entry.id)) != nil else { return nil }
    return RecognizedTool(id: entry.id, displayName: entry.displayName)
  }

  private static func loadEntries() -> [ToolLogoEntry] {
    guard
      let url = Bundle.main.url(
        forResource: "registry", withExtension: "json", subdirectory: "tool-logos"),
      let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
      let decoded = try? JSONDecoder().decode([ToolLogoEntry].self, from: data)
    else { return [] }
    return decoded
  }
}
```

```swift
import Darwin

/// The basename of `argv[0]` as a process was originally exec'd (e.g. `claude`, `vim`), or nil if it
/// can't be resolved. Deliberately NOT `proc_name`/`p_comm`: some CLIs (Claude Code among them,
/// observed in the wild) rename their own process title after launch — `p_comm` then reads as their
/// version string ("2.1.232"), not the command a user typed. `KERN_PROCARGS2` returns the ORIGINAL
/// exec-time argv snapshot, unaffected by any later self-renaming.
///
/// Shared by both PID-resolution paths in the app (issue #141): the session daemon's reattach-time
/// foreground detection (`SessionDaemon.swift`, historically the only caller) and the live-pane path
/// (`GhosttySurfaceView`'s `foregroundAgentBackend`/`foregroundTool`) — which previously used the
/// buggy `proc_name` and is fixed by switching to this shared implementation.
public enum ProcessArgv0 {
  public static func executableName(processID: pid_t) -> String? {
    guard processID > 0 else { return nil }
    var mib: [Int32] = [CTL_KERN, KERN_PROCARGS2, processID]
    var size = 0
    guard sysctl(&mib, 3, nil, &size, nil, 0) == 0, size > 4 else { return nil }
    var buffer = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: size)
    guard sysctl(&mib, 3, &buffer, &size, nil, 0) == 0, size > 4 else { return nil }
    let argc = buffer.withUnsafeBytes { $0.loadUnaligned(as: Int32.self) }
    guard argc > 0 else { return nil }
    var offset = 4
    while offset < size, buffer[offset] != 0 { offset += 1 }
    while offset < size, buffer[offset] == 0 { offset += 1 }
    guard offset < size else { return nil }
    let start = offset
    while offset < size, buffer[offset] != 0 { offset += 1 }
    guard offset > start else { return nil }
    let argv0 = String(decoding: buffer[start..<offset], as: UTF8.self)
    guard let lastSlash = argv0.lastIndex(of: "/") else { return argv0 }
    let basename = argv0[argv0.index(after: lastSlash)...]
    return basename.isEmpty ? nil : String(basename)
  }
}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fetch/refresh curated tool-logo assets (issue #141). Reads Resources/tool-logos/registry.json and,
# per entry, writes an Assets.xcassets/ToolLogo-<id>.imageset from its real favicon.
#
#   macapp/Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh            # refresh every entry
#   macapp/Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh claude gh  # refresh just these ids
#
# Highest quality first: apple-touch-icon.png (typically 180×180) → Google's public favicon proxy at
# 256px (resolves whatever a site actually declares, without this script parsing HTML) → favicon.ico
# as a last resort. ALWAYS eyeball the fetched PNGs once — Google's proxy succeeds with a generic
# globe for sites it can't resolve, so a bad fetch doesn't error, it just looks wrong.
set -euo pipefail
DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
REGISTRY="$DIR/Resources/tool-logos/registry.json"
ASSETS="$DIR/WorkroomApp/Assets.xcassets"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
ids_filter=("$@")

wanted() { [[ ${#ids_filter[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0; for w in "${ids_filter[@]}"; do [[ "$w" == "$1" ]] && return 0; done; return 1; }

fetch_source() {
  local id="$1" source="$2" domain
  domain="$(sed -E 's#^https?://##; s#/.*##' <<<"$source")"
  for url in "$source/apple-touch-icon.png" \
             "https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=$domain&sz=256" \
             "$source/favicon.ico"; do
    if curl -fsSL --max-time 10 "$url" -o "$TMP/$id.raw" 2>/dev/null \
      && [[ -s "$TMP/$id.raw" ]] \
      && sips -s format png "$TMP/$id.raw" --out "$TMP/$id.png" >/dev/null 2>&1
    then echo "  $id ← $url"; return 0; fi
  done
  return 1
}

write_imageset() {
  local id="$1" dir="$ASSETS/ToolLogo-$id.imageset"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  sips -Z 32 "$TMP/$id.png" --out "$dir/logo_32.png" >/dev/null   # -Z: proportional, not force-square
  sips -Z 64 "$TMP/$id.png" --out "$dir/logo_32@2x.png" >/dev/null
  cat >"$dir/Contents.json" <<JSON
{
  "images" : [
    { "idiom" : "universal", "scale" : "1x", "filename" : "logo_32.png" },
    { "idiom" : "universal", "scale" : "2x", "filename" : "logo_32@2x.png" }
  ],
  "info" : { "author" : "xcode", "version" : 1 }
}
JSON
}

failed=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id source; do
  wanted "$id" || continue
  if fetch_source "$id" "$source"; then write_imageset "$id"
  else echo "  $id: no favicon fetched" >&2; failed+=("$id"); fi
done < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys
for e in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])): print(f"{e[\"id\"]}\t{e[\"faviconSource\"]}")
' "$REGISTRY")

echo "Done. Eyeball the ~30 PNGs under $ASSETS/ToolLogo-*.imageset before committing —"
echo "Google's proxy succeeds silently with a generic globe for unresolvable domains."
[[ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]] && { echo "warning: no logo for: ${failed[*]}" >&2; exit 1; }
```

# Issue #141 — Favicons for terminal tabs

## Context

GitHub issue #141: terminal tabs should show a small logo icon for whatever CLI/TUI is currently
running in that pane — like a browser tab favicon — e.g. running `claude` shows the Claude logo.

Decisions already made with the user (do not relitigate):
1. **Real bundled brand logos**, fetched from each tool's actual website favicon via a script the
   user re-runs periodically to add/update the curated list — not SF Symbol placeholders.
2. **Generic detection** across a curated list of popular CLIs/TUIs (not just Claude/Codex).
3. **Placement: per-terminal tab chip only** (`TerminalTabStrip`'s `TerminalTabChip`), not the
   higher-level `WorkroomTabBar`.

Two pieces of detection machinery already exist and need no new plumbing to reach the chip:
`TerminalTab`/`TerminalState` (`TerminalSessions.swift`) already latch an `activeAgentBackend` per
tab for exactly two tools (Claude/Codex), and the tab chip already receives a full `TerminalTab` per
render. This plan generalizes the *matching* (a data-driven registry instead of two hardcoded
names) without touching the existing `AgentBackend` enum, which drives an unrelated feature (issue
#49 inline diagnosis) and must keep working unchanged.

A real correctness bug surfaces along the way: the live-pane PID→name resolution
(`AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)`, `AgentUsage.swift:139-144`) uses `proc_name`, which
Claude Code itself defeats by renaming its process title post-launch (`p_comm` reads as a version
string). The daemon's reattach-time detector (`SessionPTY.swift:154-181`) already does this
correctly via `argv[0]` (`KERN_PROCARGS2`). Expanding detection to ~30 arbitrary tools makes this
bug load-bearing (most won't have Claude's title-fallback safety net), so this plan fixes it by
sharing the daemon's argv0 helper with the live-pane path.

## Approach

### 1. Registry — single source of truth for fetch + match

New bundled JSON: `macapp/Resources/tool-logos/registry.json`, entries of `{id, displayName,
executables[], titles?, faviconSource}`. Read by both the fetch script and the app, so the "what to
fetch" list and "what to match" list can't drift apart. Bundled as a folder resource in
`project.yml` (same pattern as `Resources/markdown` at project.yml:179-181):
```yaml
- path: Resources/tool-logos
  type: folder
  buildPhase: resources
```

Starter list (30 entries) — `claude`, `codex`, `git`, `vim`(+`vi`/`view`/`gvim`), `nvim`, `tmux`,
`docker`, `kubectl`, `k9s`, `npm`(+`npx`), `node`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `bun`, `deno`, `python`(+`python3`),
`ruby`(+`irb`), `rust`(`cargo`/`rustc`), `go`, `htop`, `btop`, `lazygit`, `gh`, `redis`(`redis-cli`),
`postgres`(`psql`), `mysql`, `ssh`(+`scp`/`sftp`), `terraform`, `aws`, `curl`. `claude` is the one
entry needing `titles: ["claude code"]`, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition`'s existing literal-title
case. `btop`/`lazygit`/`tmux` have no distinct brand domain — flagged for a manual eyeball/override
pass on `faviconSource` once fetched.

### 2. New Swift: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ToolLogoRegistry.swift`

- `ToolLogoEntry: Codable` — decodes `registry.json`.
- `RecognizedTool { id, displayName }` — the small value latched onto a tab (sibling of
  `AgentBackend`, not a replacement).
- `ToolLogoRegistry.matchingEntry(forExecutableName:)` / `.matchingEntry(forTitle:)` — pure data
  match (case-sensitive on the executable-basename side, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition.backend(for:)`
  at `AgentUsage.swift:105-126`, to reject prose like "Go to definition" matching `go`).
- `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName:)` / `.tool(forTitle:)` — the gate real call sites use:
  wraps `matchingEntry` but returns `nil` unless `NSImage(named: "ToolLogo-<id>")` actually resolves,
  so a registry entry whose logo hasn't been fetched yet (or failed to fetch) never renders a
  broken/blank image.
- `ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for:)` → `"ToolLogo-<id>"`.

### 3. Fix the PID-resolution bug, sharing it app-wide

Extract `SessionPTY.swift:154-181`'s `executableName(processID:)` verbatim into a new
`macapp/WorkroomSessionProtocol/ProcessArgv0.swift` (`WorkroomSessionProtocol` is already linked
into both `WorkroomApp`, project.yml:237, and `workroom-session`, project.yml:437 — no new target
wiring needed). Delete it from `SessionPTY.swift`; update `SessionDaemon.swift`'s one call site
(~line 385) to `ProcessArgv0.executableName(processID:)`.

- `AgentUsage.swift:139-144` (`AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)`): replace the
  `proc_name`/`MAXPATHLEN` body with `backend(forProcessName: ProcessArgv0.executableName(processID: pid))`.
  This is a pure bugfix to the *existing* inline-diagnosis feature (issue #49) — `AgentBackend`/
  `AgentTitleRecognition` themselves stay untouched.
- `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:36-43` (`foregroundAgentBackend`): same underlying pid, so add a sibling
  `foregroundTool: RecognizedTool?` computed property alongside it, reusing the existing
  `foregroundProcessNameForTesting` seam:
  ```swift
  var foregroundTool: RecognizedTool? {
    if let foregroundProcessNameForTesting {
      return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: foregroundProcessNameForTesting)
    }
    guard let surface else { return nil }
    let pid = pid_t(ghostty_surface_foreground_pid(surface))
    return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: ProcessArgv0.executableName(processID: pid))
  }
  ```

### 4. Latch/clear state (mirrors the existing `activeAgentBackend` lifecycle exactly)

`TerminalSessions.swift`:
- `TerminalState` (301-324): add `var activeTool: RecognizedTool?` next to `activeAgentBackend` (314).
- `TerminalTab` (near `isRunning`, 73-76): add
  ```swift
  var recognizedTool: RecognizedTool? {
    if case .terminal(let s) = content { return s.activeTool }
    return nil
  }
  ```
- `updateTitle` (1351-1369): resolve alongside the existing agent detection and latch identically
  (first-wins, held until `command_finished`):
  ```swift
  let detectedTool = s.view.foregroundTool ?? ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forTitle: trimmed)
  guard
    s.liveTitle != trimmed || (s.activeAgentBackend == nil && detectedAgent != nil)
      || (s.activeTool == nil && detectedTool != nil)
  else { return }
  mutateTerminalState(tabID, target: target) {
    $0.liveTitle = trimmed
    if $0.activeAgentBackend == nil { $0.activeAgentBackend = detectedAgent }
    if $0.activeTool == nil { $0.activeTool = detectedTool }
  }
  ```
- `handleCommandFinished` (1396-1408): also clear `$0.activeTool = nil`.

Scope note: this is a first-wins latch like `activeAgentBackend` — the icon doesn't swap mid-command
if the foreground process changes under one shell prompt; it swaps *between* commands. Inside tmux,
the pane's foreground pgid is tmux itself, so a `tmux` pane shows the tmux logo, not the inner
program's — same accepted limitation the existing agent-detection comment already notes for
multiplexed sessions.

### 5. Render — `TerminalTabStrip.swift`, `TerminalTabChip.body`

New block in the existing content-kind-glyph slot, after the changeset glyph (516-521) and before
the unread-activity dot (522-529) — the slot that today renders nothing for plain `.terminal` tabs:
```swift
if let tool = tab.recognizedTool {
  Image(ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for: tool.id))
    .resizable()
    .aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit)
    .frame(width: 12, height: 12)
    .help(tool.displayName)
    .accessibilityLabel(tool.displayName)
}
```
`.aspectRatio(.fit)` matters — fetched favicons won't all be perfectly square. This is an ordinary
HStack element (affects measured chip width via `TabWidthKey`, 631-638), same category as the
existing diff/file/changeset glyphs — no new width-measurement risk.

### 6. Fetch/update script — `macapp/Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh`

Bash, following `vendor-markdown.sh`'s conventions (curl + `python3 -c` for JSON, no new
dependency). Reads `registry.json`; per entry, tries `<site>/apple-touch-icon.png` → Google's public
favicon proxy (`s2/favicons?domain=…&sz=256`) → `<site>/favicon.ico`; converts via `sips` to a
32pt/@2x PNG pair; writes `Assets.xcassets/ToolLogo-<id>.imageset/` (non-template, full color —
**not** copying `MenuBarIcon.imageset`'s `template-rendering-intent: template` flag, only its
folder/`Contents.json` structuring convention). Supports refreshing a subset: `fetch-tool-logos.sh
claude gh`. Prints a reminder to eyeball the fetched PNGs — the Google proxy succeeds silently with
a generic globe for domains it can't resolve.

Add a `make app-tool-logos` target (Makefile, mirrors `app-icon` at line ~130) and its `.PHONY` entry.

No checksum manifest (unlike `vendor-markdown.sh`'s `VENDOR.md`) — that exists there because
DOMPurify is security-critical; these are decorative brand icons, so a checksum ledger is
unrequested complexity.

### 7. Sequencing caveat

Steps 1-5 (registry, Swift code, chip rendering, tests) are fully implementable and testable now —
with zero imagesets present, `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(...)` returns `nil` everywhere and the chip
renders nothing, which is correct (not broken). **Running the fetch script itself needs real network
access to each tool's homepage domain** (`claude.ai`, `git-scm.com`, `neovim.io`, `www.google.com`
for the proxy fallback, etc.) — none of which are in this session's sandboxed network allowlist, so
that step runs with the sandbox disabled, as its own explicit step, not silently bundled into the
main implementation. After fetching: eyeball the ~30 PNGs (script prints this reminder), fix up
`btop`/`lazygit`/`tmux` if they came back as generic globes, commit the imagesets, `make app-generate
&& make app-test`.

### 8. Tests

New `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/ToolLogoRegistryTests.swift` (mirrors `AgentUsageTests.swift`'s shape):
alias matching (`vim`/`vi`/`nvim` full-path basename resolution), case-sensitivity, title
first-token matching, false-positive rejection (`"Go to definition"`, `"Ruby on Rails guide"` must
not match), unrecognized name/title → `nil`. Test only the pure `matchingEntry` functions, not the
image-gated `tool(...)` wrappers (those depend on which imagesets happen to be committed at test
time). Run via `make app-test`.

Regression check: `AgentUsageTests.swift`'s existing Claude/Codex PID-recognition test must still
pass post-bugfix (it exercises the same `AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)` path now backed
by `ProcessArgv0` instead of `proc_name`).

## Verification

- `make app-test` — new `ToolLogoRegistryTests` + existing `AgentUsageTests` regression.
- `make app-lint` on all touched/new files.
- Manual, end-to-end (needs `make app-tool-logos` run first with sandbox disabled, so real logos
  exist to see): open terminal tabs and run a few long-running tools from the list one at a time
  (`claude`, `nvim`, `htop`, `lazygit`, `psql`) — confirm each chip shows the right logo + `.help`
  tooltip, confirm the icon persists per-tab when switching between tabs, confirm it clears back to
  nothing at the next shell prompt (`command_finished`), confirm an unrecognized command shows no
  icon, and confirm the ✦ inline-diagnosis badge still appears correctly for a running `claude`
  (post-bugfix regression check on the unrelated issue #49 feature).

2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Pros / cons:
```
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Writing Style (skip entirely if `EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse` appears in the preamble echo OR the user's current message explicitly requests terse / no-explanations output)

Applies to AskUserQuestion, user replies, and findings. AskUserQuestion Format is structure; this is prose quality.

- Gloss curated jargon on first use per skill invocation, even if the user pasted the term.
- Frame questions in outcome terms: what pain is avoided, what capability unlocks, what user experience changes.
- Use short sentences, concrete nouns, active voice.
- Close decisions with user impact: what the user sees, waits for, loses, or gains.
- User-turn override wins: if the current message asks for terse / no explanations / just the answer, skip this section.
- Terse mode (EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse): no glosses, no outcome-framing layer, shorter responses.

Curated jargon list lives at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/jargon-list.json` (80+ terms). On the first jargon term you encounter this session, Read that file once; treat the `terms` array as the canonical list. The list is repo-owned and may grow between releases.


## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Confusion Protocol

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.

Before ANYTHING else in this skill — before the Design Doc Check, the office-hours prerequisite offer, Step 0, and any `git` / `Read` / `Grep` / `Glob` / `Bash` call — unless an exception below applies, your VERY FIRST tool call MUST be AskUserQuestion, to confirm the review target. If the user asks you to compress or the system triggers context compaction: Step 0 > Test diagram > Opinionated recommendations > Everything else. Never skip Step 0 or the test diagram. Do not preemptively warn about context limits -- the system handles compaction automatically.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).
* I err on the side of handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed.
* Bias toward explicit over clever.
* Right-sized diff: favor the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change ... but don't compress a necessary rewrite into a minimal patch. If the existing foundation is broken, say "scrap it and do this instead."

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

## Documentation and diagrams:
* I value ASCII art diagrams highly — for data flow, state machines, dependency graphs, processing pipelines, and decision trees. Use them liberally in plans and design docs.
* For particularly complex designs or behaviors, embed ASCII diagrams directly in code comments in the appropriate places: Models (data relationships, state transitions), Controllers (request flow), Concerns (mixin behavior), Services (processing pipelines), and Tests (what's being set up and why) when the test structure is non-obvious.
* **Diagram maintenance is part of the change.** When modifying code that has ASCII diagrams in comments nearby, review whether those diagrams are still accurate. Update them as part of the same commit. Stale diagrams are worse than no diagrams — they actively mislead. 184	Code coverage isn't enough — you need to cover how real users interact with the changed code. For each changed feature, think through:
185	
186	- **User flows:** What sequence of actions does a user take that touches this code? Map the full journey (e.g., "user clicks 'Pay' → form validates → API call → success/failure screen"). Each step in the journey needs a test.
187	- **Interaction edge cases:** What happens when the user does something unexpected?
188	  - Double-click/rapid resubmit
189	  - Navigate away mid-operation (back button, close tab, click another link)
190	  - Submit with stale data (page sat open for 30 minutes, session expired)
191	  - Slow connection (API takes 10 seconds — what does the user see?)
192	  - Concurrent actions (two tabs, same form)
193	- **Error states the user can see:** For every error the code handles, what does the user actually experience?
194	  - Is there a clear error message or a silent failure?
195	  - Can the user recover (retry, go back, fix input) or are they stuck?
196	  - What happens with no network? With a 500 from the API? With invalid data from the server?
197	- **Empty/zero/boundary states:** What does the UI show with zero results? With 10,000 results? With a single character input? With maximum-length input?
198	
199	Add these to your diagram alongside the code branches. A user flow with no test is just as much a gap as an untested if/else.
200	
201	**Step 3. Check each branch against existing tests:**
202	
203	Go through your diagram branch by branch — both code paths AND user flows. For each one, search for a test that exercises it:
204	- Function `processPayment()` → look for `billing.test.ts`, `billing.spec.ts`, `test/billing_test.rb`
205	- An if/else → look for tests covering BOTH the true AND false path
206	- An error handler → look for a test that triggers that specific error condition
207	- A call to `helperFn()` that has its own branches → those branches need tests too
208	- A user flow → look for an integration or E2E test that walks through the journey
209	- An interaction edge case → look for a test that simulates the unexpected action
210	
211	Quality scoring rubric:
212	- ★★★  Tests behavior with edge cases AND error paths
213	- ★★   Tests correct behavior, happy path only
214	- ★    Smoke test / existence check / trivial assertion (e.g., "it renders", "it doesn't throw")

216	### E2E Test Decision Matrix
217	
218	When checking each branch, also determine whether a unit test or E2E/integration test is the right tool:
219	
220	**RECOMMEND E2E (mark as [→E2E] in the diagram):**
221	- Common user flow spanning 3+ components/services (e.g., signup → verify email → first login)
222	- Integration point where mocking hides real failures (e.g., API → queue → worker → DB)
223	- Auth/payment/data-destruction flows — too important to trust unit tests alone
224	
225	**RECOMMEND EVAL (mark as [→EVAL] in the diagram):**
226	- Critical LLM call that needs a quality eval (e.g., prompt change → test output still meets quality bar)
227	- Changes to prompt templates, system instructions, or tool definitions
228	
229	**STICK WITH UNIT TESTS:**
230	- Pure function with clear inputs/outputs
231	- Internal helper with no side effects
232	- Edge case of a single function (null input, empty array)
233	- Obscure/rare flow that isn't customer-facing
234	
235	### REGRESSION RULE (mandatory)
236	
237	**IRON RULE:** When the coverage audit identifies a REGRESSION — code that previously worked but the diff broke — a regression test is added to the plan as a critical requirement. No AskUserQuestion. No skipping. Regressions are the highest-priority test because they prove something broke.
238	
239	A regression is when:
240	- The diff modifies existing behavior (not new code)
241	- The existing test suite (if any) doesn't cover the changed path
242	- The change introduces a new failure mode for existing callers
243	
244	When uncertain whether a change is a regression, err on the side of writing the test.

1	# Issue #141 — Favicons for terminal tabs
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	GitHub issue #141: terminal tabs should show a small logo icon for whatever CLI/TUI is currently
6	running in that pane — like a browser tab favicon — e.g. running `claude` shows the Claude logo.
7	
8	Decisions already made with the user (do not relitigate):
9	1. **Real bundled brand logos**, fetched from each tool's actual website favicon via a script the
10	   user re-runs periodically to add/update the curated list — not SF Symbol placeholders.
11	2. **Generic detection** across a curated list of popular CLIs/TUIs (not just Claude/Codex).
12	3. **Placement: per-terminal tab chip only** (`TerminalTabStrip`'s `TerminalTabChip`), not the
13	   higher-level `WorkroomTabBar`.
14	
15	Two pieces of detection machinery already exist and need no new plumbing to reach the chip:
16	`TerminalTab`/`TerminalState` (`TerminalSessions.swift`) already latch an `activeAgentBackend` per
17	tab for exactly two tools (Claude/Codex), and the tab chip already receives a full `TerminalTab` per
18	render. This plan generalizes the *matching* (a data-driven registry instead of two hardcoded
19	names) without touching the existing `AgentBackend` enum, which drives an unrelated feature (issue
20	#49 inline diagnosis) and must keep working unchanged.
21	
22	A real correctness bug exists nearby but is **out of scope for this plan** (scope-reduction decision,
23	D1): the live-pane PID→name resolution (`AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)`,
24	`AgentUsage.swift:139-144`) uses `proc_name`, which Claude Code itself defeats by renaming its
25	process title post-launch (`p_comm` reads as a version string). The daemon's reattach-time detector
26	(`SessionPTY.swift:154-181`) already does this correctly via `argv[0]` (`KERN_PROCARGS2`). This bug
27	is already safety-netted today — `AgentTitleRecognition`'s title-based fallback catches Claude
28	regardless (that's how the ✦ diagnosis badge, issue #49, already works correctly) — and the new
29	favicon feature's own Claude/Codex matching uses the identical fallback pattern
30	(`ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forTitle:)`), so the favicon renders correctly for Claude with or without
31	this fix. Bundling the fix would have pulled 3 extra files across 2 extra targets
32	(`WorkroomSession`, `WorkroomSessionProtocol`) into this PR for a bug this feature doesn't actually
33	have — deferred instead as its own TODOS.md entry (§7).
34	
35	## Approach
36	
37	### 1. Registry — single source of truth for fetch + match
38	
39	New bundled JSON: `macapp/Resources/tool-logos/registry.json`, entries of `{id, displayName,
40	executables[], titles?, faviconSource}`. Read by both the fetch script and the app, so the "what to
41	fetch" list and "what to match" list can't drift apart. Bundled as a folder resource in
42	`project.yml` (same pattern as `Resources/markdown` at project.yml:179-181):
43	```yaml
44	- path: Resources/tool-logos
45	  type: folder
46	  buildPhase: resources
47	```
48	
49	Starter list (30 entries) — `claude`, `codex`, `git`, `vim`(+`vi`/`view`/`gvim`), `nvim`, `tmux`,
50	`docker`, `kubectl`, `k9s`, `npm`(+`npx`), `node`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `bun`, `deno`, `python`(+`python3`),
51	`ruby`(+`irb`), `rust`(`cargo`/`rustc`), `go`, `htop`, `btop`, `lazygit`, `gh`, `redis`(`redis-cli`),
52	`postgres`(`psql`), `mysql`, `ssh`(+`scp`/`sftp`), `terraform`, `aws`, `curl`. `claude` is the one
53	entry needing `titles: ["claude code"]`, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition`'s existing literal-title
54	case. `btop`/`lazygit`/`tmux` have no distinct brand domain — flagged for a manual eyeball/override
55	pass on `faviconSource` once fetched.
56	
57	### 2. New Swift: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ToolLogoRegistry.swift`
58	
59	- `ToolLogoEntry: Codable` — decodes `registry.json`.
60	- `RecognizedTool { id, displayName }` — the small value latched onto a tab (sibling of
61	  `AgentBackend`, not a replacement).
62	- `ToolLogoRegistry.matchingEntry(forExecutableName:)` / `.matchingEntry(forTitle:)` — pure data
63	  match (case-sensitive on the executable-basename side, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition.backend(for:)`
64	  at `AgentUsage.swift:105-126`, to reject prose like "Go to definition" matching `go`).
65	- `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName:)` / `.tool(forTitle:)` — the gate real call sites use:
66	  wraps `matchingEntry` but returns `nil` unless `NSImage(named: "ToolLogo-<id>")` actually resolves,
67	  so a registry entry whose logo hasn't been fetched yet (or failed to fetch) never renders a
68	  broken/blank image.
69	- `ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for:)` → `"ToolLogo-<id>"`.
70	- `loadEntries()` logs on failure (CQ2) — a static `Logger` (mirrors `GhosttySurfaceView.sessionLogger`'s
71	  declaration) with an `.error` call distinguishing "resource not found" from "decode failed," so a
72	  broken `registry.json` (bad project.yml wiring, a JSON typo, a future schema break) surfaces in
73	  Console.app instead of silently disabling every favicon with zero signal.
74	
75	### 3. Resolve the foreground tool — reuses today's `proc_name` path (bugfix deferred, §7)
76	
77	`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:36-43` (`foregroundAgentBackend`): add a sibling `foregroundTool:
78	RecognizedTool?` computed property, resolving the same pid the same way `foregroundAgentBackend`
79	already does — `proc_name` via `AgentProcessRecognition`-style lookup, NOT a new shared argv0
80	helper (that unification is the deferred bugfix, §7). Reuses the existing
81	`foregroundProcessNameForTesting` seam:
82	  ```swift
83	  var foregroundTool: RecognizedTool? {
84	    if let foregroundProcessNameForTesting {
85	      return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: foregroundProcessNameForTesting)
86	    }
87	    guard let surface else { return nil }
88	    var name = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: Int(MAXPATHLEN))
89	    let pid = pid_t(ghostty_surface_foreground_pid(surface))
90	    guard pid > 1, proc_name(pid, &name, UInt32(name.count)) > 0 else { return nil }
91	    return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: String(cString: name))
92	  }
93	  ```
94	  Same known limitation as today's `foregroundAgentBackend` for any tool that renames its own
95	  process title (confirmed case: Claude) — safety-netted by the title-fallback in `updateTitle`
96	  (§4), identical to how issue #49's diagnosis badge already tolerates this.
97	
98	### 4. Latch/clear state (mirrors the existing `activeAgentBackend` lifecycle exactly)
99	
100	`TerminalSessions.swift`:
101	- `TerminalState` (301-324): add `var activeTool: RecognizedTool?` next to `activeAgentBackend` (314).
102	- `TerminalTab` (near `isRunning`, 73-76): add
103	  ```swift
104	  var recognizedTool: RecognizedTool? {
105	    if case .terminal(let s) = content { return s.activeTool }
106	    return nil
107	  }
108	  ```
109	- `updateTitle` (1351-1369): resolve alongside the existing agent detection and latch identically
110	  (first-wins, held until `command_finished`):
111	  ```swift
112	  let detectedTool = s.view.foregroundTool ?? ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forTitle: trimmed)
113	  guard
114	    s.liveTitle != trimmed || (s.activeAgentBackend == nil && detectedAgent != nil)
115	      || (s.activeTool == nil && detectedTool != nil)
116	  else { return }
117	  mutateTerminalState(tabID, target: target) {
118	    $0.liveTitle = trimmed
119	    if $0.activeAgentBackend == nil { $0.activeAgentBackend = detectedAgent }
120	    if $0.activeTool == nil { $0.activeTool = detectedTool }
121	  }
122	  ```
123	- `handleCommandFinished` (1396-1408): also clear `$0.activeTool = nil`.
124	
125	Scope note: this is a first-wins latch like `activeAgentBackend` — the icon doesn't swap mid-command
126	if the foreground process changes under one shell prompt; it swaps *between* commands. Inside tmux,
127	the pane's foreground pgid is tmux itself, so a `tmux` pane shows the tmux logo, not the inner
128	program's — same accepted limitation the existing agent-detection comment already notes for
129	multiplexed sessions.
130	
131	### 5. Render — `TerminalTabStrip.swift`, `TerminalTabChip.body`
132	
133	New block in the existing content-kind-glyph slot, after the changeset glyph (516-521) and before
134	the unread-activity dot (522-529) — the slot that today renders nothing for plain `.terminal` tabs:
135	```swift
136	if let tool = tab.recognizedTool {
137	  Image(ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for: tool.id))
138	    .resizable()
139	    .aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit)
140	    .frame(width: 12, height: 12)
141	    .help(tool.displayName)
142	    .accessibilityLabel(tool.displayName)
143	    .accessibilityIdentifier("terminal.tool.\(tool.id)")
144	}
145	```
146	`.aspectRatio(.fit)` matters — fetched favicons won't all be perfectly square. This is an ordinary
147	HStack element (affects measured chip width via `TabWidthKey`, 631-638), same category as the
148	existing diff/file/changeset glyphs — no new width-measurement risk. The `.accessibilityIdentifier`
149	(T2) mirrors the existing ✦ agentBadge's own identifier (`terminal.agentBadge`,
150	`TerminalTabStrip.swift:485`) — both exist so XCUITest can query the glyph reliably.
151	
152	### 6. Fetch/update script — `macapp/Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh`
153	
154	Bash, following `vendor-markdown.sh`'s conventions (curl + `python3 -c` for JSON, no new
155	dependency). Reads `registry.json`; per entry, tries `<site>/apple-touch-icon.png` → Google's public
156	favicon proxy (`s2/favicons?domain=…&sz=256`) → `<site>/favicon.ico`; converts via `sips` to a
157	32pt/@2x PNG pair; writes `Assets.xcassets/ToolLogo-<id>.imageset/` (non-template, full color —
158	**not** copying `MenuBarIcon.imageset`'s `template-rendering-intent: template` flag, only its
159	folder/`Contents.json` structuring convention). Supports refreshing a subset: `fetch-tool-logos.sh
160	claude gh`. Prints a reminder to eyeball the fetched PNGs — the Google proxy succeeds silently with
161	a generic globe for domains it can't resolve.
162	
163	Add a `make app-tool-logos` target (Makefile, mirrors `app-icon` at line ~130) and its `.PHONY` entry.
164	
165	No checksum manifest (unlike `vendor-markdown.sh`'s `VENDOR.md`) — that exists there because
166	DOMPurify is security-critical; these are decorative brand icons, so a checksum ledger is
167	unrequested complexity.
168	
169	### 7. Deferred — file as a TODOS.md entry, not part of this PR
170	
171	Add a TODOS.md entry (same style as the existing `ghostty_surface_tty_name is available and unused`
172	entry) naming the `proc_name`→argv0 unification: `AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)`
173	(`AgentUsage.swift:139-144`) and the new `foregroundTool` (§3) both resolve a live pane's foreground
174	process via `proc_name`, which Claude Code defeats by renaming its own process title post-launch —
175	the daemon's reattach path (`SessionPTY.swift:154-181`) already resolves this correctly via
176	`argv[0]`/`KERN_PROCARGS2`. Follow-up: extract that logic into a shared
177	`WorkroomSessionProtocol` helper and use it from both `AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)` and
178	`foregroundTool`. Priority P3 — no known bug today (title-fallback safety-nets both call sites); worth
179	doing next time either recognizer needs to get sturdier.
180	
181	### 8. Sequencing caveat
182	
183	Steps 1-5 (registry, Swift code, chip rendering, tests) are fully implementable and testable now —
184	with zero imagesets present, `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(...)` returns `nil` everywhere and the chip
185	renders nothing, which is correct (not broken). **Running the fetch script itself needs real network

1. **The sequencing claim is false.** `foregroundTool` calls the image-gated `tool(...)`. With zero imagesets, T1 cannot latch `"git"` and T2 cannot render it. Asset fetching is a prerequisite for integration testing. Move asset gating to rendering.

2. **The reused state machine has the wrong semantics.** Agent detection tracks long-lived Claude/Codex sessions. A favicon claiming “currently running” cannot be first-wins per shell command. Wrappers and child transitions (`sudo → vim`, `npm → node`, `git → pager`) will show the wrong tool or none.

3. **Detection depends on incidental title-change timing.** There is no guarantee a command causes `updateTitle`, or that it fires after the foreground PID changes. The plan needs a command-start/foreground-process observation mechanism, not title repaint as its clock.

4. **The state machine has an idle re-latch race.** `command_finished` can clear the icon, then a late/stale title update can immediately restore it. Nothing checks that the tab is still running. Detection needs a command generation/running-state guard.

5. **Stale icons have no recovery path.** If `command_finished` is missed—unsupported shell integration, reattach, abrupt process exit—the first-wins latch can survive indefinitely and block future tools. Additional clearing triggers are required.

6. **T2 is intrinsically flaky.** `git status` usually exits before XCUITest can observe a 12px element. Use a deterministic long-running fixture or a controlled test executable with synchronization.

7. **The tests model behavior production does not have.** Full-path basename tests exercise injected strings, while production uses `proc_name`, with different truncation/name semantics. Versioned executables, shims, `env`, `sudo`, package runners, and symlinks remain untested.

8. **The “single source of truth” claim is wrong.** Registry entries and imagesets are independently committed and can drift. The runtime gate merely hides missing assets. Add validation for missing/orphan assets, duplicate IDs, duplicate aliases, invalid IDs, and malformed sources.

9. **The fetch pipeline is nondeterministic and weakly validated.** Root-level icon guesses and Google’s proxy can return cached, generic, obsolete, HTML, or low-resolution results. “Eyeball 30 files” is not a reliable update process. Validate MIME type, dimensions, transparency, source URL, and conversion success.

10. **Redistribution rights are ignored.** Publicly accessible favicons are not automatically licensed for bundling and redistribution. Thirty third-party trademarks create a release/legal dependency the plan never sequences.

11. **The visual treatment is incomplete.** `.aspectRatio(.fit)` does not address dark-mode invisibility, transparent padding, tiny source upscaling, inconsistent optical size, or illegibility at 12pt.

12. **The starter catalog is badly calibrated.** Many entries (`git`, `curl`, `aws`, `terraform`) are normally too short-lived for users to perceive. The plan assumes the maintenance cost of 30 brands before proving the mechanism on long-running agents and TUIs.

# Issue #141 — Favicons for terminal tabs

## Context

GitHub issue #141: terminal tabs should show a small logo icon for whatever CLI/TUI is currently
running in that pane — like a browser tab favicon — e.g. running `claude` shows the Claude logo.

Decisions already made with the user (do not relitigate):
1. **Real bundled brand logos**, fetched from each tool's actual website favicon via a script the
   user re-runs periodically to add/update the curated list — not SF Symbol placeholders.
2. **Generic detection** across a curated list of popular CLIs/TUIs (not just Claude/Codex).
3. **Placement: per-terminal tab chip only** (`TerminalTabStrip`'s `TerminalTabChip`), not the
   higher-level `WorkroomTabBar`.

Two pieces of detection machinery already exist and need no new plumbing to reach the chip:
`TerminalTab`/`TerminalState` (`TerminalSessions.swift`) already latch an `activeAgentBackend` per
tab for exactly two tools (Claude/Codex), and the tab chip already receives a full `TerminalTab` per
render. This plan generalizes the *matching* (a data-driven registry instead of two hardcoded
names) without touching the existing `AgentBackend` enum, which drives an unrelated feature (issue
#49 inline diagnosis) and must keep working unchanged.

A real correctness bug exists nearby but is **out of scope for this plan** (scope-reduction decision,
D1): the live-pane PID→name resolution (`AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:)`,
`AgentUsage.swift:139-144`) uses `proc_name`, which Claude Code itself defeats by renaming its
process title post-launch (`p_comm` reads as a version string). The daemon's reattach-time detector
(`SessionPTY.swift:154-181`) already does this correctly via `argv[0]` (`KERN_PROCARGS2`). This bug
is already safety-netted today — `AgentTitleRecognition`'s title-based fallback catches Claude
regardless (that's how the ✦ diagnosis badge, issue #49, already works correctly) — and the new
favicon feature's own Claude/Codex matching uses the identical fallback pattern
(`ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forTitle:)`), so the favicon renders correctly for Claude with or without
this fix. Bundling the fix would have pulled 3 extra files across 2 extra targets
(`WorkroomSession`, `WorkroomSessionProtocol`) into this PR for a bug this feature doesn't actually
have — deferred instead as its own TODOS.md entry (§7).

## Approach

### 1. Registry — single source of truth for fetch + match

New bundled JSON: `macapp/Resources/tool-logos/registry.json`, entries of `{id, displayName,
executables[], titles?, faviconSource}`. Read by both the fetch script and the app, so the "what to
fetch" list and "what to match" list can't drift apart. Bundled as a folder resource in
`project.yml` (same pattern as `Resources/markdown` at project.yml:179-181):
```yaml
- path: Resources/tool-logos
  type: folder
  buildPhase: resources
```

Starter list (30 entries) — `claude`, `codex`, `git`, `vim`(+`vi`/`view`/`gvim`), `nvim`, `tmux`,
`docker`, `kubectl`, `k9s`, `npm`(+`npx`), `node`, `yarn`, `pnpm`, `bun`, `deno`, `python`(+`python3`),
`ruby`(+`irb`), `rust`(`cargo`/`rustc`), `go`, `htop`, `btop`, `lazygit`, `gh`, `redis`(`redis-cli`),
`postgres`(`psql`), `mysql`, `ssh`(+`scp`/`sftp`), `terraform`, `aws`, `curl`. `claude` is the one
entry needing `titles: ["claude code"]`, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition`'s existing literal-title
case. `btop`/`lazygit`/`tmux` have no distinct brand domain — flagged for a manual eyeball/override
pass on `faviconSource` once fetched.

### 2. New Swift: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ToolLogoRegistry.swift`

- `ToolLogoEntry: Codable` — decodes `registry.json`.
- `RecognizedTool { id, displayName }` — the small value latched onto a tab (sibling of
  `AgentBackend`, not a replacement).
- `ToolLogoRegistry.matchingEntry(forExecutableName:)` / `.matchingEntry(forTitle:)` — pure data
  match (case-sensitive on the executable-basename side, mirroring `AgentTitleRecognition.backend(for:)`
  at `AgentUsage.swift:105-126`, to reject prose like "Go to definition" matching `go`).
- `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName:)` / `.tool(forTitle:)` — the gate real call sites use:
  wraps `matchingEntry` but returns `nil` unless `NSImage(named: "ToolLogo-<id>")` actually resolves,
  so a registry entry whose logo hasn't been fetched yet (or failed to fetch) never renders a
  broken/blank image.
- `ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for:)` → `"ToolLogo-<id>"`.
- `loadEntries()` logs on failure (CQ2) — a static `Logger` (mirrors `GhosttySurfaceView.sessionLogger`'s
  declaration) with an `.error` call distinguishing "resource not found" from "decode failed," so a
  broken `registry.json` (bad project.yml wiring, a JSON typo, a future schema break) surfaces in
  Console.app instead of silently disabling every favicon with zero signal.

### 3. Resolve the foreground tool — reuses today's `proc_name` path (bugfix deferred, §7)

`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:36-43` (`foregroundAgentBackend`): add a sibling `foregroundTool:
RecognizedTool?` computed property, resolving the same pid the same way `foregroundAgentBackend`
already does — `proc_name` via `AgentProcessRecognition`-style lookup, NOT a new shared argv0
helper (that unification is the deferred bugfix, §7). Reuses the existing
`foregroundProcessNameForTesting` seam:
  ```swift
  var foregroundTool: RecognizedTool? {
    if let foregroundProcessNameForTesting {
      return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: foregroundProcessNameForTesting)
    }
    guard let surface else { return nil }
    var name = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: Int(MAXPATHLEN))
    let pid = pid_t(ghostty_surface_foreground_pid(surface))
    guard pid > 1, proc_name(pid, &name, UInt32(name.count)) > 0 else { return nil }
    return ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName: String(cString: name))
  }
  ```
  Same known limitation as today's `foregroundAgentBackend` for any tool that renames its own
  process title (confirmed case: Claude) — safety-netted by the title-fallback in `updateTitle`
  (§4), identical to how issue #49's diagnosis badge already tolerates this.

### 4. Latch/clear state (mirrors the existing `activeAgentBackend` lifecycle exactly)

`TerminalSessions.swift`:
- `TerminalState` (301-324): add `var activeTool: RecognizedTool?` next to `activeAgentBackend` (314).
- `TerminalTab` (near `isRunning`, 73-76): add
  ```swift
  var recognizedTool: RecognizedTool? {
    if case .terminal(let s) = content { return s.activeTool }
    return nil
  }
  ```
- `updateTitle` (1351-1369): resolve alongside the existing agent detection and latch identically
  (first-wins, held until `command_finished`):
  ```swift
  let detectedTool = s.view.foregroundTool ?? ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forTitle: trimmed)
  guard
    s.liveTitle != trimmed || (s.activeAgentBackend == nil && detectedAgent != nil)
      || (s.activeTool == nil && detectedTool != nil)
  else { return }
  mutateTerminalState(tabID, target: target) {
    $0.liveTitle = trimmed
    if $0.activeAgentBackend == nil { $0.activeAgentBackend = detectedAgent }
    if $0.activeTool == nil { $0.activeTool = detectedTool }
  }
  ```
- `handleCommandFinished` (1396-1408): also clear `$0.activeTool = nil`.

Scope note: this is a first-wins latch like `activeAgentBackend` — the icon doesn't swap mid-command
if the foreground process changes under one shell prompt; it swaps *between* commands. Inside tmux,
the pane's foreground pgid is tmux itself, so a `tmux` pane shows the tmux logo, not the inner
program's — same accepted limitation the existing agent-detection comment already notes for
multiplexed sessions.

### 5. Render — `TerminalTabStrip.swift`, `TerminalTabChip.body`

New block in the existing content-kind-glyph slot, after the changeset glyph (516-521) and before
the unread-activity dot (522-529) — the slot that today renders nothing for plain `.terminal` tabs:
```swift
if let tool = tab.recognizedTool {
  Image(ToolLogoRegistry.assetName(for: tool.id))
    .resizable()
    .aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit)
    .frame(width: 12, height: 12)
    .help(tool.displayName)
    .accessibilityLabel(tool.displayName)
    .accessibilityIdentifier("terminal.tool.\(tool.id)")
}
```
`.aspectRatio(.fit)` matters — fetched favicons won't all be perfectly square. This is an ordinary
HStack element (affects measured chip width via `TabWidthKey`, 631-638), same category as the
existing diff/file/changeset glyphs — no new width-measurement risk. The `.accessibilityIdentifier`
(T2) mirrors the existing ✦ agentBadge's own identifier (`terminal.agentBadge`,
`TerminalTabStrip.swift:485`) — both exist so XCUITest can query the glyph reliably.

### 6. Fetch/update script — `macapp/Scripts/fetch-tool-logos.sh`

Bash, following `vendor-markdown.sh`'s conventions (curl + `python3 -c` for JSON, no new
dependency). Reads `registry.json`; per entry, tries `<site>/apple-touch-icon.png` → Google's public
favicon proxy (`s2/favicons?domain=…&sz=256`) → `<site>/favicon.ico`; converts via `sips` to a

Add a `make app-tool-logos` target (Makefile, mirrors `app-icon` at line ~130) and its `.PHONY` entry.

No checksum manifest (unlike `vendor-markdown.sh`'s `VENDOR.md`) — that exists there because

### 7. Deferred — file as a TODOS.md entry, not part of this PR

1. **The sequencing claim is false.** `foregroundTool` calls the image-gated `tool(...)`. With zero imagesets, T1 cannot latch `"git"` and T2 cannot render it. Asset fetching is a prerequisite for integration testing. Move asset gating to rendering.

2. **The reused state machine has the wrong semantics.** Agent detection tracks long-lived Claude/Codex sessions. A favicon claiming “currently running” cannot be first-wins per shell command. Wrappers and child transitions (`sudo → vim`, `npm → node`, `git → pager`) will show the wrong tool or none.

3. **Detection depends on incidental title-change timing.** There is no guarantee a command causes `updateTitle`, or that it fires after the foreground PID changes. The plan needs a command-start/foreground-process observation mechanism, not title repaint as its clock.

4. **The state machine has an idle re-latch race.** `command_finished` can clear the icon, then a late/stale title update can immediately restore it. Nothing checks that the tab is still running. Detection needs a command generation/running-state guard.

5. **Stale icons have no recovery path.** If `command_finished` is missed—unsupported shell integration, reattach, abrupt process exit—the first-wins latch can survive indefinitely and block future tools. Additional clearing triggers are required.

6. **T2 is intrinsically flaky.** `git status` usually exits before XCUITest can observe a 12px element. Use a deterministic long-running fixture or a controlled test executable with synchronization.

7. **The tests model behavior production does not have.** Full-path basename tests exercise injected strings, while production uses `proc_name`, with different truncation/name semantics. Versioned executables, shims, `env`, `sudo`, package runners, and symlinks remain untested.

8. **The “single source of truth” claim is wrong.** Registry entries and imagesets are independently committed and can drift. The runtime gate merely hides missing assets. Add validation for missing/orphan assets, duplicate IDs, duplicate aliases, invalid IDs, and malformed sources.

9. **The fetch pipeline is nondeterministic and weakly validated.** Root-level icon guesses and Google’s proxy can return cached, generic, obsolete, HTML, or low-resolution results. “Eyeball 30 files” is not a reliable update process. Validate MIME type, dimensions, transparency, source URL, and conversion success.

10. **Redistribution rights are ignored.** Publicly accessible favicons are not automatically licensed for bundling and redistribution. Thirty third-party trademarks create a release/legal dependency the plan never sequences.

11. **The visual treatment is incomplete.** `.aspectRatio(.fit)` does not address dark-mode invisibility, transparent padding, tiny source upscaling, inconsistent optical size, or illegibility at 12pt.

12. **The starter catalog is badly calibrated.** Many entries (`git`, `curl`, `aws`, `terraform`) are normally too short-lived for users to perceive. The plan assumes the maintenance cost of 30 brands before proving the mechanism on long-running agents and TUIs.

Cross-checking against the review already done — most are either already-explicit accepted limitations in the plan (first-wins mid-command, title-change-as-clock, missed-`command_finished` staleness — all shared with the already-shipped `activeAgentBackend` feature, not new) or minor/non-actionable (proc_name truncation semantics). **CROSS-MODEL TENSION:**
- **Sequencing bug**: Codex is right — T1/T2 as I specified them call the *image-gated* `tool(...)` path, but §8 claims tests are "fully implementable and testable now" with zero imagesets. Those two claims contradict each other.
- **T2 flakiness**: `git status` exits too fast for XCUITest to reliably observe a 12px glyph — needs a long-running invocation like the existing precedent test uses.
- **No duplicate-id/alias validation**: registry.json has no check against two entries claiming the same `id` or the same executable alias (silent last-write-wins).
- **Trademark/redistribution risk**: bundling ~30 third-party brand logos into a notarized, distributed macOS app is a real business/legal call — not mine to silently accept.
- **Dark/light theme legibility**: nothing in the plan addresses whether arbitrary fetched favicons stay legible across this app's many themes.
- **Starter-list calibration**: several entries (git, curl, aws, terraform) are typically too short-lived for a user to ever see the icon.

questions.question:
X1 — Sequencing bug (Codex, confirmed real): T1/T2 call the image-gated path but §8 claims tests work with zero imagesets.
`foregroundTool` → `ToolLogoRegistry.tool(forExecutableName:)`, which returns nil unless `NSImage(named: "ToolLogo-git")` actually resolves (§2's whole point — never render a broken/missing image). Stakes if we pick wrong: CI/local `make app-test` fails on a fresh clone until a human manually runs a network-dependent fetch script — or worse, someone "fixes" it by weakening the tests to bypass the image gate, defeating the whole point of §2's gate (never render broken images).
Recommendation: A) fetch + commit just ONE real icon (git's) as part of THIS PR's implementation step (one network call, not the bulk 30-icon run) — because it's the smallest fix that keeps T1/T2 testing the REAL gated path with a real asset, and doesn't touch the gate's semantics.
Completeness: A=9/10 (tests prove the real path, deterministic, no CI dependency on the bulk fetch script), B=4/10 (ships with tests that fail on a fresh checkout until a human separately runs a network script).

questions.question:
TODO 1 — proc_name→argv0 unification for foreground-process detection.
What: extract SessionPTY.swift's argv0/KERN_PROCARGS2 executableName logic into a shared WorkroomSessionProtocol helper, and use it from both AgentProcessRecognition.backend(forPID:) (issue #49 diagnosis) and the new foregroundTool (issue #141 favicon) — replacing both call sites' current proc_name usage.
Why: proc_name is defeated by any CLI that renames its own process title post-launch (confirmed case: Claude Code, whose p_comm becomes a version string). Currently safety-netted by title-based fallback in both features, so no user-visible bug today — but every new tool added to the favicon registry is one more surface where this could matter if it also self-renames.
Pros: sturdier detection long-term; consolidates two near-duplicate PID-resolution code paths into one; the daemon side already proves the fix works (its reattach path already does this correctly).
Cons: touches 3 files across 2 targets (WorkroomSession, WorkroomSessionProtocol) for a bug with no known live symptom today — exactly why it was deferred out of this PR (D1).
Context: this session already produced the reasoning — see plan §7 (deferred TODOS.md entry) and D1 for the full scope-reduction rationale. Depends on nothing; can land any time.

questions.question:
TODO 2 — Automated validation for the fetch-tool-logos.sh pipeline.
What: add MIME-type/dimension/generic-globe detection to fetch-tool-logos.sh, instead of relying purely on a human eyeballing ~30 PNGs before committing.
Why: Codex's outside-voice review flagged that Google's favicon proxy fallback can silently return a generic globe icon (or a stale/cached/low-res result) for a domain it can't resolve, and the script currently has no automated check for that — only a printed reminder to look at the files.
Pros: catches a bad fetch automatically instead of relying on a human not missing it among 30 files; makes future re-runs (adding new tools) safer as the list grows past 30.
Cons: real added complexity (image dimension/hash checks, generic-globe fingerprinting) for a script that already has a working manual safeguard (the eyeball pass, now also checking light/dark legibility per X5) — arguably over-engineering a personal/small-team dev-maintenance script.
Context: no urgency — the manual eyeball step already exists and this session added a theme-legibility check to it (X5). This would upgrade that from "manual only" to "automated + manual."

- Manual, end-to-end (needs `make app-tool-logos` run first with sandbox disabled, so real logos
  exist to see): open terminal tabs and run a few long-running tools from the list one at a time
  (`claude`, `nvim`, `htop`, `lazygit`, `psql`) — confirm each chip shows the right logo + `.help`
  tooltip, confirm the icon persists per-tab when switching between tabs, confirm it clears back to
  nothing at the next shell prompt (`command_finished`), and confirm an unrecognized command shows no
  icon.

## NOT in scope

- **proc_name→argv0 unification** — deferred (D1), filed as a TODOS.md follow-up (§7, TODO1
  accepted). No known live bug today; the title-fallback safety net covers Claude/Codex.
- **Automated fetch-pipeline validation** (MIME/dimension/generic-globe detection in
  `fetch-tool-logos.sh`) — considered and declined (TODO2): the manual eyeball pass (now also
  checking theme legibility, X5) is sufficient for a low-frequency, single-maintainer script.
- **Favicon on `WorkroomTabBar`** (the workroom-level tab, aggregating multiple terminal panes) —
  scoped out from the start (placement decision): ambiguous when panes run different tools, no clear
  priority rule for which icon would win.
- **Trimming the starter registry to only long-running tools** — considered (X6), kept as-is: the
  fetch script is cheaply re-runnable, so there's no real cost to a few low-visibility entries now.

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

- `activeAgentBackend`/`TerminalState`/`TerminalTab` latch-clear lifecycle (`TerminalSessions.swift`)
  — REUSED as the exact template for `activeTool`'s lifecycle (first-wins latch, cleared on
  `command_finished`), not reimplemented.
- `AgentTitleRecognition`/`AgentProcessRecognition`'s case-sensitive first-token matching
  (`AgentUsage.swift`) — REUSED as the template for `ToolLogoRegistry.matchingEntry` (the pattern is
  copied, not the code itself, since `AgentBackend` stays untouched per the D1 scope decision).
- `MenuBarIcon.imageset` — the one existing bundled (non-SF-Symbol) image precedent — REUSED for the
  imageset/`Contents.json` folder convention (not its `template-rendering-intent`, which is for
  single-color tinted icons; these need full color).
- `vendor-markdown.sh` — REUSED for the fetch script's curl + `python3 -c` JSON-parsing conventions.
- `Resources/markdown`'s folder-resource wiring in `project.yml` — REUSED as the pattern for
  `Resources/tool-logos`.
- `foregroundProcessNameForTesting` test seam (`GhosttySurfaceView`) — REUSED by `foregroundTool`,
  no new test seam needed.
- `GhosttyActionDispatchUITests`/`testCodexAgentSurvivesProviderTitleRepaint` — REUSED as the direct
  templates for T2 and T1 respectively.

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Failure scenario | Test? | Error handling? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loadEntries()` decode | Bad `project.yml` wiring, JSON typo, schema break | No | Yes (CQ2: logs via os.Logger) | Nothing (no icons anywhere) — degrades to pre-feature behavior, not a crash |
| `foregroundTool`/`proc_name` | Dead pid, restricted process, name unresolved | No (matches existing `foregroundAgentBackend` behavior) | Yes (guard chain → nil) | Nothing (chip shows no icon) |
| `tool(forExecutableName/forTitle:)` image gate | Registry entry exists, imageset not yet fetched | Yes (unrecognized-path tests) | Yes, by design (§2) | Nothing — correct, not broken |
| registry.json duplicate id/alias | Copy-paste mistake in a future edit | Yes (X3, new) | N/A (test catches it pre-merge) | N/A |
| Missed `command_finished` (reattach, abrupt exit) | Stale icon persists past command end | No — shared, pre-existing risk with `activeAgentBackend` | No (same as today) | Stale icon until next tab action — not a new regression |
| Fetched icon illegible in a theme | White/dark-on-transparent art vs. arbitrary chip fill | No (manual, X5) | Manual eyeball-pass check | Icon may be invisible in one theme mode until caught in review |

No new **critical gaps** (no test AND no error handling AND silent) remain after this review's fixes
— the closest candidate (silent registry decode failure) now has logging (CQ2), and the missed-
`command_finished` staleness risk is inherited unchanged from the already-shipped `activeAgentBackend`
feature, not introduced by this plan.

## Worktree parallelization strategy

| Step | Modules touched | Depends on |
|------|-----------------|------------|
| Registry + matching layer | `Resources/tool-logos/`, `WorkroomApp/Core/ToolLogoRegistry.swift` | — |
| Foreground detection wiring | `WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift` | Registry + matching layer |
| Latch/clear state | `WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift` | Foreground detection wiring |
| Chip rendering | `WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift` | Latch/clear state |
| Fetch script + build wiring | `Scripts/`, `project.yml`, `Makefile` | Registry schema only |
| Tests | `WorkroomAppTests/`, `WorkroomAppUITests/` | All of the above |

Two independent workstreams exist (Swift logic vs. fetch script/build wiring), so a worktree split is
technically possible — but at 9 files total for one small feature, the coordination overhead isn't
worth it. **Sequential implementation recommended**, no parallelization.
